form-client-ssh-pass-input-tip-sub: Windows, Linux and macOS all support SSH keys and passwords against a verified host key. The password belongs only to the address, port and account given here; a change of identity needs it again, and no public key is registered for you. Leaving the password empty while editing keeps the password saved for that identity.

hb-docker-h3: Keep a proxy enabled for a remote account
hb-docker-p: Register a Linux node or a container in the node management view with its SSH user, host and real port. A Windows controller uses an OpenSSH key. The Docker host mode also needs that account to run docker exec. Save it and run the pre-check first.
hb-docker-p-2: The tool and shell configuration is written only when you enable it explicitly. The target is the selected account or container, and running as root can also change system-wide settings on the target. Stopping restores the snapshot. When the file was edited by hand or an older version left no snapshot, read the notice and check the backup.
hb-win-p: Run it in the extracted folder of the portable archive. Bash and curl must already be installed. The source archive also needs Python 3.8 or newer.
hb-win-strong: One command on Linux or macOS
local-gateway-panel-p: The tool ships with an observation gateway that listens only on this machine, so you can try the whole proxy flow right away.

setup-title-p: Enter the host and HTTP or mixed port of a proxy that is already running. The console sends the requests from the machine it runs on, so use 127.0.0.1 for a proxy on the same machine.

step-1-explain: Select an HTTP or mixed proxy gateway the target node can reach. The button below sends a request from the console through that gateway.
step-1-result-res-msg: Click Probe to check whether the gateway port and service answer. Step 2 unlocks once the check succeeds.
step-2-explain: Choose the worker node that needs proxy access (edge node, workstation, or another host), or register a new one below:
step-3-explain: The console will request the configured target sites through the selected gateway and record each HTTP status and latency.
tab-handbook-card-subdesc: First save an existing HTTP or mixed proxy gateway in the wizard and click Send a proxy request. After an HTTP 2xx, choose one of the usages below.
tab-handbook-p: Open PowerShell in the extracted folder of the portable archive. The script uses the bundled Python and sets the proxy for this one curl command.

wizard-compare: Repeat the same GET with the system curl
wizard-feedback-content-li: After it is enabled, curl, wget, pip and Git in the target account can read their own proxy settings. Programs that depend on shell variables should be checked in a new terminal.
wizard-feedback-content-li-2: When the managed state stops, the tool restores the configuration from the snapshot taken before it was enabled. A proxy that already existed may still apply, so repeat the request with a plain curl to check the current path.
wizard-feedback-content-li-3: The container mode runs the configuration script inside the selected container. Running it as root can change system-wide settings on the target; when the restoration conflicts, check the files on the target.
wizard-feedback-content-reference-summar: 🛠️ Advanced commands and code reference (for advanced developers; not needed in daily use)
wizard-target-disp-sub: The account or the container appears here once you choose a target.
